title: MarinerLink SI hybrid plugin discovery
summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood and MarinerLink to evaluate a hybrid SI plugin that enables MarinerLink to resell Redwood Dedicated/private deployments. Main concerns: networking/VPC integration, key management (KMS/HSM), tenant isolation, and predictable latency for batch inference. Agreed next steps: send security pack and pilot pricing, schedule benchmark, MarinerLink to provide sample workload.
next_steps: Lena Park - Send security whitepaper + SOC2 summary (by 2026-04-01)
Omar Ruiz - Draft benchmark plan and sample Redwood config (by 2026-04-03)
Priya Menon - Share pilot workload + sizing targets (by 2026-04-02)
Schedule follow-up technical deep dive with MarinerLink infra team (w/in 2 weeks)
action_items: Lena Park - Share pricing and pilot spec - 2026-04-01
Omar Ruiz - Prepare benchmark plan and sample config - 2026-04-03
Priya Menon - Provide sample workload and test dataset - 2026-04-02

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~53 minutes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Priya (MarinerLink), Jonas (MarinerLink), Ellen (MarinerLink)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Intro + discovery for SI hybrid plugin / reseller flow. High-level infra constraints noted. Security checklist requested. Pilot agreed pending workload and pricing.

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining; can you hear me okay?
[00:05] Priya: Yeah loud and clear, thanks Lena.
[00:07] Jonas: Good to be here.
[00:10] Lena: Cool. Quick intros — I'm Lena Park, AE on the partnerships team at Redwood. Omar's our solutions engineer, he'll steer the technical bits.
[00:18] Omar: Hi all. I'll mostly talk infra and ops, and sketch how the SI plugin would sit in a hybrid flow.
[00:24] Priya: I'm Priya, lead partnerships at MarinerLink, and Jonas here is our SI lead who'll own integration. Ellen is our security architect.
[00:32] Ellen: Hey.

[00:35] Lena: Great. Goal for today — understand MarinerLink's reseller model and constraints, talk about Redwood Dedicated and Private options, and surface any blockers for a bundled plugin or onramp offering. We'll also capture pilot scope. Does that sound right?
[00:45] Priya: Yup, that works. We're trying to figure out whether we can package Redwood as a managed option for our customers — some want hosted and others need on-prem or VPC routing.

[01:00] Jonas: To kick off, high-level context: MarinerLink is a systems integrator focused on telco and logistics verticals. We resell cloud infra and provide managed ML infra. Our customers need predictable latency, we do multi-tenant overlays, and some customers require on-prem or air-gapped options. We're exploring an integration where we can deploy Redwood behind our management plane and have an easy license / onboarding flow for our customers.

[01:20] Omar: Helpful, thanks. Can you share your typical deployment patterns? Are you planning to run Redwood Dedicated instances in your own DCs, or enable a flow where customers choose hosted vs on-prem?
[01:30] Jonas: Mostly a mix. For smaller customers they prefer hosted; mid-market/enterprise want private VPC deployments, sometimes on-prem. For telco customers we often need an on-prem appliance model.

[01:45] Priya: Important for us: we want a single control plane in MarinerLink to spin up customer accounts, configure defaults, and set routing policies — e.g., if latency SLO < 100ms route to Dedicated in-region, else fall back to hosted.

[02:02] Omar: That maps well to Redwood's smart routing and model variants. We support policy-based routing and fallbacks; you can pin model versions per-customer. The nuance for a reseller flow is auth and tenant isolation: do you want MarinerLink to manage keys and networking, or have Redwood's control plane manage those?

[02:20] Ellen: Security perspective: we need KMS/HSM integration, SSO for our ops console, audit logs, and clear data residency guarantees. SOC 2 is required for our customers in NA, and ISO27001 for some EU customers.

[02:36] Lena: Totally. We have enterprise packages for Private deployments with customer-managed VPC and KMS. For Dedicated we offer reserved capacity and optional VPC peering; audit logs and SAML/SSO are available. We'll share our security whitepaper.

[02:50] Jonas: Two quick questions right away: first, can you support nested tenancy — like MarinerLink has tenants and they, in turn, have customer tenants — and second, what's the latency hit for a Dedicated private deployment vs hosted?

[03:05] Omar: For tenancy, Redwood supports hierarchical account models through our routing and tenancy metadata — you can create an umbrella reseller account and then subaccounts for customers; RBAC maps to that. There are some ops considerations around billing flows. For latency, it depends on GPU type and batch sizing; on high-end A100-class GPUs we generally hit single-digit token latencies for short context lengths; with batching you'll trade latency for throughput.

[03:35] Priya: Hmm, single-digit token latencies sounds optimistic; our telco customers want end-to-end under 100ms for short responses. How realistic is that when you add network hops and a MarinerLink control plane in the middle?

[03:48] Omar: Good point — network plus proxying adds. If you colocate in the same region and use direct peering or private interconnect, you can still be under 100ms for small generative requests. Otherwise, you'll need edge or a local Dedicated pool. We can discuss placement strategies.

[04:05] Jonas: On the plugin itself, our goal is to have a MarinerLink-managed UI where partners can choose Redwood options and we orchestrate the deployment. We don't want to rebuild model serving. So ideally Redwood exposes APIs for programmatic provisioning and a billing export.

[04:22] Lena: We have programmatic APIs for model provisioning, route configs, and usage. Billing exports and per-token usage are available. One thing to note — for reseller flows we usually sign an MSP-style contract that defines who owns the customer SLA and who we invoice.

[04:35] Priya: Who typically owns support? We like to keep first line support, but deeper infra issues should go to Redwood.

[04:42] Lena: That's our usual pattern: reseller handles triage and first-level fixes, Redwood handles platform and model regressions. We can propose an escalation matrix.

[04:50] Ellen: On encryption, for Private deployments do you support customer-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys, and can we enforce in-transit and at-rest? Also need to retain logs for 12 months for some customers.

[05:05] Omar: Yes — customer-managed KMS is supported for Private; for Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS via connectors or require envelope encryption. We log at token-level and request-level; retention windows can be configured but longer retention is an add-on. We'll include specifics in the security pack.

[05:24] Jonas: Are there any known limitations for NVMe caching or the KV cache when you run on-prem? We have customers doing long context chats with KV caches and we worry about memory constraints.

[05:36] Omar: The runtime manages KV cache; on-prem you can size cache nodes. For very large context, we recommend LRU policies and sometimes offload cold state to a vector DB. Some transcription errors in prior docs call it 'K-V cash' but it's KV cache.

[05:50] Priya: Haha yes we've seen the K-V cash note. Another concern: when we resell, some customers will want us to alter model weights or run custom fine-tuning. Does Redwood permit model modifications on Dedicated?

[06:04] Lena: We support serving custom model artifacts in Private/Dedicated if you provide the artifact or we can assist with onboarding. There are guardrails for provenance and compatibility checks. Fine-tuning is typically a separate workflow; we can help with hosting tuned checkpoints for serving.

[06:22] Jonas: On pricing — we need a ballpark for pilot: say 3-4 mid-market customers, intermittent peak usage. What is the typical commitment for a Dedicated pilot?

[06:34] Lena: For pilot we usually propose a 3-month trial with a modest reserved pool (e.g., 1-2 GPUs depending on workload) and uplifts for bursts. Pricing depends on GPU class and whether you want private control plane. We'll send a pilot pricing sheet.

[06:48] Priya: Ok we'll need that. Also we want an API for license provisioning so our UI can spin up seats.

[06:55] Omar: That's doable. We'll map the provisioning API to your tenant model. There are rate limits to consider; if you expect high churn we can adjust.

[07:08] Ellen: Let me surface compliance items — we cannot accept data exfil logs being shipped outside region, and we need proof of encryption at rest with customer KMS. Also require periodic pen-test reports.

[07:22] Lena: Noted. We'll include SOC 2 report, our pen test summary, and options for regional-only deployments.

[07:30] Jonas: For integration timeline, if we want a pilot in July, what's realistic for provisioning, contract, and benchmarks?

[07:38] Lena: A June contract to start a July pilot is reasonable. We can do a small benchmark in April/May to validate latency and cost projections assuming you provide sample traffic.

[07:50] Priya: Speaking of sample traffic: Jonas will put together typical request shapes and token distributions. Does Redwood need raw logs or anonymized data?

[07:59] Omar: Anonymized is fine; we just need representative payload sizes, sequence lengths, and concurrency. If you can include 95th percentile request sizes and target latency SLOs that helps sizing.

[08:12] Jonas: Got it. We'll aim to deliver that by next week.

[08:16] Lena: Great. Omar, can you walk through a possible architecture sketch for MarinerLink's hybrid plugin?

[08:21] Omar: Sure — I'll share screen after this (note: screen share referenced). High-level: MarinerLink control plane talks to Redwood provisioning API to create a customer-specific routing policy and model pin. For private deployments, MarinerLink will either manage a VPC with the Redwood control plane peering in, or Redwood will ship a private control plane deployed in MarinerLink's environment. Traffic path options: direct peering (best latency), reverse-proxy through MarinerLink (easier for multi-tenant routing), or edge pop placement for very low latency.

[08:52] Jonas: If we do reverse-proxy, we need to understand TLS cert management and token auth.

[08:58] Omar: We support mTLS between control plane components; tokens are short-lived and you can integrate SAML/OIDC for operator SSO. Certs can be uploaded or we can integrate with your cert manager.

[09:10] Ellen: How do you handle audit logs for customer tenant events — are they available as push to our logging infra or pull from Redwood?

[09:18] Omar: Both. We can push to syslog/S3 or expose APIs to pull logs. For long-term retention and to meet your compliance needs, push to your logging endpoint is typical.

[09:27] Priya: A couple of sticky points we anticipate: 1) billing integration, 2) support SLAs, and 3) upgrade window planning so customers don't get rollbacks during peak. Any thoughts?

[09:39] Lena: Billing — we can do metered exports and monthly invoices to MarinerLink. SLAs — reseller can have separate SLA tiers; Redwood supports escalation and outage credits in enterprise contracts. Upgrades — we have rollouts with canaries and automatic fallback to previous model versions to reduce blast radius.

[09:58] Jonas: On the technical deep dive, we might want an SE-led session focused on performance: batching strategies, quantization, and kernel selection since some customers will want lower cost at slightly higher latency.

[10:10] Omar: Absolutely — we can demo how Optimize suggests quantization and batching configs per workload and show the kernel selection impact. We can also run a tiny benchmark to show cost/latency curves.

[10:24] Priya: That will be helpful for our commercial deck. Also: competitors — we've looked at CloudSphere and VertexLane; main differences we're evaluating are pricing and deployment flexibility.

[10:36] Lena: Understood. We'll include a comparison matrix in the follow-up.

[10:41] Jonas: Another detail: are there any licensing restrictions around model catalogs? Some customers want only vetted open models, others want proprietary models.

[10:50] Omar: Redwood maintains a model catalog and you can restrict the catalog per-customer. Hosting proprietary models is supported on Private/Dedicated; we validate compatibility but don't lock you out.

[10:59] Ellen: For EU data residency, can we ensure logs and model artifacts remain in region? We have a customer in Germany that requires both.

[11:08] Omar: Yes regional deployments are available; the private control plane can be deployed in your EU region so artifacts and logs never leave the region.

[11:16] Priya: Great. Let's talk briefly about the pilot acceptance criteria — what would Redwood consider success?

[11:22] Lena: From our side, success is: 1) validate we can meet your customers' latency SLOs for selected workloads; 2) confirm billing/invoicing works; 3) confirm security/compliance controls are in place; and 4) collect qualitative feedback from MarinerLink ops on onboarding and management APIs.

[11:36] Jonas: We'll add: 95th latency below 120ms for our chosen workloads, and clear indicators on cost per 1k tokens.

[11:44] Ellen: Also need log retention and proof of KMS integration for the pilot.

[11:49] Omar: Noted. We'll include those in the benchmark plan.

[11:53] Priya: Any immediate red flags from Redwood side for the reseller model?

[11:58] Lena: Nothing blocking — it's mostly contract and operational choices: who manages keys, who pays for GPUs, and support tier definitions.

[12:08] Jonas: Ok sounds fair. For timelines — we'll aim to get sample traffic to you by 2026-04-02, and we'll reconvene for a perf deep dive the week after.

[12:18] Lena: Works for us. Omar, can you follow up with a benchmark template and sample request shapes so they know what to send?

[12:24] Omar: Yep, will do.

[12:26] Priya: One last thing: do you have any references for other SIs who've integrated Redwood?

[12:31] Lena: We can share a reference list and some case studies — e.g., a telco integration and an enterprise SI flow. I'll include those links in the follow-up.

[12:40] Jonas: Perfect.

[12:42] Ellen: Thanks everyone.

[12:45] Lena: Thanks all. Quick recap of next steps: Lena will send security pack and pilot pricing, Omar will send benchmark plan, Priya/Jonas will provide sample workload. We'll schedule technical deep dive for performance within two weeks.

[12:58] Priya: Sounds good, thank you.

[13:02] Jonas: Thanks.

[13:05] Lena: Bye.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., 'K-V cash' instead of KV cache), some speaker labels collapsed (Speaker 3 instead of name in sections of the original auto-transcript), natural speech hesitations preserved.

References mentioned: "pilot pricing sheet" (link placeholder: https://redwood.example/pilot-pricing), "security whitepaper" (link placeholder: https://redwood.example/security), "benchmark template" (to be shared by Omar).
